Evidence: Freedom of navigation, Choke point capture, Strategic entrapment
#Aletheia #Yemen #Geopolitics

Washington maintains that its strategic stockpile and deterrence remain fully intact, projecting steady regional security and freedom of navigation.

Stated Judgement: (+0.76, +0.65) — Greater Good

Houthi control of Perim Island gives Tehran leverage over both global oil conduits, cornering US policy between domestic inflation and combat overextension.

Resulting Judgement: (-0.92, -0.74) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Destruction.
Escalating economic coercion without viable ground alternatives locks the US military into an intractable maritime quagmire.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 24.30, z: 0)

Houthi forces reached Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, jeopardizing Red Sea commerce while Washington grapples with rising domestic gas prices and multi-front naval friction.

Projecting supreme geopolitical control preserves face, but it prevents leadership from admitting strategic limits before a full shipping shutdown strikes.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The breakdown contrasts narrative bravado with physical reality. Officials claim unlimited capacity, yet maritime trade channels are physically blocked on the water.

Social Physics Analysis:
The administration runs a Smart Selfish stall: project total military dominance to ward off political blowback over gas prices. But ignoring logistical reality allows opponents to seize geographic choke points, turning manufactured pretexts into real crises.

The Trajectory: The Path of Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Coercive hubris drives systemic breakdown.

The Unavoidable Truth: Controlling narrow straits gives asymmetric forces massive leverage over global trade.

The Unavoidable Lie: Naval operations can endlessly absorb new fronts without economic blowback.

Alethekanon:

Awwthekanon:
Ordinary families caught between soaring energy costs and endless overseas conflict pay the real price whenever leaders refuse to acknowledge their limits.

Brothekanon:
Officials keep saying everything is under control, but oil ships cannot pass and gas prices are spiking. You cannot bluff your way through a locked shipping lane.
